cases.oracle: Boot the inline game from demos/minicraft/index.html in a vm sandbox with DOM/canvas/localStorage stubs and drive the real pointerdown/pointerup handlers on the same stone (type 3) cell: TYPES[1].hardness==1, TYPES[2].hardness==1, TYPES[3].hardness==3, TYPES[4].hardness==3; hit 1 leaves grid[cell]==3 with damage==1 and exactly one visible crack stage whose draw is a pure deterministic function of (x,y,stage); hit 2 leaves grid[cell]==3 with damage==2 and a distinct second crack stage; hit 3 sets grid[cell]==0, deletes the damage entry and inventory[3]==1 exactly, with a canvas HUD fillText showing the incremented stone count in the top-right quadrant. Wood (type 4) shows the identical 3-hit removal and inventory[4]==1. Same-cell pointermove never adds a hit (damage accrues on cell-entry edges only). Inventory stays a non-negative integer for types 1..4 throughout.

One pointerdown/pointerup on a grass (type 1) cell sets grid[cell]==0, inventory[1]==1, creates no damage entry and draws no crack strokes; the same single click on a dirt (type 2) cell removes it with inventory[2]==1; digging an already-empty cell is a no-op: grid, inventory and the exact saved localStorage blob string are all unchanged.

Digging one block of each type 1..4 accrues exactly +1 of that type (inventory[t]==1 after the hardness-th hit); selecting the type from the palette and right-click-placing on the emptied cell writes type t back and decrements that type's inventory by exactly 1 (1->0); with stock 0 the placement is refused before any mutation: target cell stays 0, inventory deep-equals its previous value and the saved blob string is byte-identical; after a type reaches 0 every palette swatch greys out (opacity 0.35).

After shaping the world (one stone, one grass and one wood destroyed plus a second stone cracked to stage 2) storage holds exactly one localStorage key whose parsed blob deep-equals {version:2, cells:<400-entry grid>, inventory:{1:1,2:0,3:1,4:1}} with keys exactly [cells,inventory,version] and no damage field; a fresh boot on the same storage restores grid and inventory deep-equal with a transient empty damage map and the cracked stone intact; boot on empty storage yields the default 20x20 world and inventory all-zero {1:0,2:0,3:0,4:0}. A stored legacy v1 blob {version:1, cells} migrates on load with inventory defaulted to 0 for every type while the world cells are restored.

cleanup.environment: Each check runs node --test in a short-lived child process on the repo worktree; tests load the inline game script into a node:vm sandbox with DOM/canvas/localStorage stubs. No daemons, ports, browsers, global env or settings files are touched.
cleanup.data: localStorage is a per-boot in-memory Map stub discarded with the sandbox; no files, real localStorage or persistent state are written, so no data cleanup is required.
